advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_declared_compose_services distinguish 'compose file absent' from 'services healthy' — emit a countable marker (or return nonzero) instead of `return 0` when the expected compose file is missing.
evidence: COMPOSE_DIR defaults to $DEPLOY_REPO/infra/compose (autodeploy.sh:42); if DEPLOY_REPO is misconfigured/empty or the checkout is incomplete, the file is absent and the check returns 0 with no marker
The check produces its 'clean' verdict both when all services run AND when it never actually looked (file missing) — it cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'check never ran'
advisory.finding: check_declared_compose_services() returns success (0) whenever $COMPOSE_DIR/docker-compose.yml is absent or misnamed, so the declared-service liveness check silently no-ops and autodeploy still reports 'up to date; no-op'. Absence of the file is indistinguishable from 'all declared services running' — the exact fail-open class this ticket exists to close.
scenarios: DEPLOY_REPO points at an empty/partial checkout on a box
compose file is renamed to compose.yaml/docker-compose.yaml
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the silent `return 0` with an err marker + return 1 (e.g. err compose-file-missing "$COMPOSE_DIR/docker-compose.yml absent"), or gate the check's applicability on a positive signal that the deploy tree is present.

dropped.finding: The test does not assert the process exit code, so the newly-added `check_declared_compose_services || exit 1` clause (the commit's 'exits nonzero instead of a healthy no-op' contract) is regression-blind: if `|| exit 1` were removed, the marker would still be emitted and every assertion would pass while the script exits 0.
merged_from: No happy-path / negative test covers the case where all declared services are running: check_declared_compose_services must NOT emit AUTODEPLOY_ERROR and the tick must exit 0 as a clean no-op. Nothing verifies the check stays silent on a healthy box.
scenarios: The `|| exit 1` wiring is dropped or the function's `return 1` is lost, but marker emission is preserved — test stays green while the unattended loop reports success.
